incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Royal Legislative Decree 1/2010 approving the Spanish Companies Act (Ley de Sociedades de Capital), principally Articles 19-23, 28-30, 58-62, 78-81, 210-212, 214-216, 221, and 279-284; Royal Decree 1784/1996 approving the Commercial Registry Regulations; Law 14/2013 and related implementing rules for electronic incorporation through CIRCE where eligible.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: The Central Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil Central) for company-name certification and the competent Provincial Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil Provincial) for registration of the company and its deed.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Public deed of incorporation (escritura pública de constitución) executed before a Spanish notary and filed with the competent Provincial Mercantile Registry, supported by the Central Mercantile Registry name certificate and the company bylaws.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: A Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada may be incorporated with minimum share capital of EUR 1. Capital must be fully subscribed and paid at incorporation. Until equity reaches EUR 3,000, at least 20% of annual profit must be allocated to legal reserve until the reserve plus capital reaches EUR 3,000, and shareholder liability on liquidation is subject to the statutory minimum-capital protection rule. A separate statutory escrow account is not required; any bank certificate of contribution is subject to applicable notarial and banking practice.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The Board resolves that: (1) the subscribed share capital of EUR [amount], divided into [number] shares of EUR [nominal value] each, is acknowledged as fully subscribed and paid by the sole shareholder(s); (2) the registered office at [full Spanish address] is adopted; (3) [name] is appointed sole director, or [names] are appointed as directors, each accepting office and declaring eligibility; (4) the appointed officer(s) are authorized to obtain the company tax identification number, complete Mercantile Registry filings, open bank accounts, and execute all documents necessary to commence lawful operations; and (5) the corporate books and beneficial-ownership records shall be maintained in accordance with Spanish law.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Central Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil Central), online name-certification service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit up to five proposed names, identify the applicant, pay the applicable registry charge, and obtain the certificate of no identical name. The certificate is generally valid for three months for execution of the deed and six months for name reservation, subject to applicable registry rules.
required_dossiers: Power of attorney if filed by an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Submit alternative names if rejected for identity, similarity, prohibited wording, or formal defect; correct the application and request a new certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Foreign Shareholder and Director Identification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish Tax Agency (Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria), through the applicable NIE and NIF procedures
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain an NIE for each non-Spanish individual director or shareholder and an NIF for each foreign corporate shareholder. Applications may be filed in Spain or through a Spanish consulate, subject to consular procedure. Foreign corporate documents must be legalized or apostilled and accompanied by sworn Spanish translations where required.
required_dossiers: Foreign corporate certificate of incorporation and current registry extract
Apostille or legalization and sworn Spanish translation where applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Cure missing identification, representation, legalization, translation, or address evidence and resubmit to the Tax Agency or competent consular office.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish notary selected by the incorporator; CIRCE/PAE platform where electronic incorporation is used
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the public deed, bylaws, shareholder details, capital structure, registered office, corporate purpose, management system, and beneficial-ownership information. Ensure the corporate purpose covers wholesale food and botanical products, import-export, storage, and related lawful activities without replacing required sector registrations.
required_dossiers: Capital contribution evidence or founders' declaration as accepted by the notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct notarial observations, clarify the corporate purpose or management structure, and execute an amended or corrected deed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execute the Public Deed and Pay Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The incorporator(s) execute the escritura pública de constitución. Pay the subscribed capital into the company's formation bank account or provide the legally accepted contribution declaration. The notary verifies identity, authority, corporate name, bylaws, capital, beneficial ownership, and statutory formalities.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Rectify documentary defects identified by the notary and re-execute or supplement the deed before filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Provisional Tax Identification and File the Deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish Tax Agency and competent Provincial Mercantile Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Request the provisional company NIF using Form 036 or the applicable CIRCE workflow, then submit the notarized deed electronically or physically to the Provincial Mercantile Registry for registration. Pay the applicable registry and publication charges; no single nationwide fee is denominated in USD.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to the registrar's defect notice within the prescribed period, submit a corrective deed where necessary, and re-present the corrected filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete Post-Registration Tax and Beneficial-Ownership Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish Tax Agency, Provincial Mercantile Registry, and applicable electronic corporate-record systems
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain the definitive NIF, update tax registration, select VAT and intra-Community transaction registrations where relevant, and maintain the shareholders' register, minutes book, accounting books, and beneficial-ownership information. Apply for VIES registration before intra-Community transactions requiring it.
required_dossiers: Electronic certificate or authorized filing credential
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct tax-registration inconsistencies, provide additional activity or address evidence, and appeal or refile according to Tax Agency procedures.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register the Food Business and Organic Activity
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish Agency for Food Safety and Nutrition (AESAN) and the competent food authority of the autonomous community where the establishment operates; Organic production authority or authorized control body
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Determine whether the activity requires entry in the General Sanitary Registry of Food and Food Companies (RGSEAA) or an autonomous-community food-business communication or registration. File before commencing regulated operations. If products are marketed as organic, register with the competent organic control authority and use required certification, traceability, and import documentation.
required_dossiers: Food-safety self-control system based on HACCP principles
Organic certificate or control-body application where applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to the food authority's information request, correct the activity classification, and do not commence the regulated activity until the required communication, registration, or authorization is effective.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Secure Municipal Premises and Safety Authorizations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipality (Ayuntamiento) of the premises and the competent autonomous-community industrial, fire, and environmental authorities
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm zoning compatibility for food storage and wholesale use. File the municipal activity declaration, prior communication, or licence required by local ordinance. Obtain or retain technical certificates for fire protection, occupancy, electrical installations, refrigeration, structural loads, accessibility, and workplace safety as applicable.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Cure municipal technical observations, submit revised plans, request inspection, and use the applicable administrative appeal or review procedure against a refusal.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: The competent autonomous-community industry and environmental department, together with the municipality where the warehouse or facility is located. Spain has no single nationwide manufacturing licence applicable to every food wholesaler; requirements depend on storage, processing, packaging, refrigeration, emissions, and local activity classification.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Municipal activity and opening licence or prior responsible declaration (licencia de actividad y apertura or declaración responsable), plus food-business registration or prior communication with RGSEAA or the competent autonomous-community food authority where applicable.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry for the Ecological Transition and the Demographic Challenge (Ministerio para la Transición Ecológica y el Reto Demográfico), with the competent autonomous-community environmental authority as the ordinary project authority
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Ordinary dried-herb wholesale storage in an existing facility is generally outside the Annex I and Annex II project categories of Law 21/2013 and normally requires no standalone EIA. Processing, substantial new construction, major refrigeration installations, waste treatment, or protected-site impacts may trigger screening or a full EIA under Law 21/2013 and autonomous-community rules.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Comply with applicable municipal and autonomous-community wastewater discharge limits, Industrial Emissions legislation where relevant, air-quality and volatile-organic-compound requirements for installed equipment, and waste legislation including Law 7/2022. Food and plant waste, packaging, hazardous waste, refrigerants, and pest-control residues must be segregated, documented, and transferred to authorized operators. Site-specific permit conditions control numerical thresholds.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Before operation, obtain the municipal or competent-authority fire-safety approval or responsible declaration required for the premises, supported by a qualified technical project and inspection. Verify structural load capacity for pallet racking and stored goods, emergency routes, fire detection and extinguishing systems, electrical safety, refrigeration safety, and accessibility. Implement Law 31/1995 occupational risk-prevention obligations, including risk assessment, training, emergency planning, personal protective equipment, and contractor controls. Pressure equipment, lifts, refrigeration systems, and other regulated installations require applicable registration and periodic inspections.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) - State Tax Administration Agency; electronic headquarters 'Sede Electrónica de la AEAT' at https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es; customs authority: Departamento de Aduanas e Impuestos Especiales de la AEAT.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: execute the SL incorporation deed before a notary and register at the Mercantile Registry; Step 2: obtain the provisional corporate NIF from the approved notary or registry; Step 3: within 30 days of incorporation, file Form 036 (Censo de Obligados Tributarios) at the competent AEAT delegation, attaching the registry certificate, statutory bylaws and Spanish tax domicile, to obtain the definitive corporate NIF (CIF/NIF); Step 4: simultaneously enrol in the IVA (VAT) census to receive the VAT identification number (NIF-IVA), and register for the IAE local activity tax if in scope; Step 5: obtain an X.509 digital certificate (FNMT or electronic DNI) for mandatory electronic filings; Step 6: foreign shareholders must hold a NIF-UE (EU residents) or a non-resident NIF (non-EU) obtained via Form 036 and may appoint a Spanish tax representative. Non-established foreign exporters claiming Spanish VAT refunds must register through the AEAT electronic gateway and appoint a fiscal representative when required.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; the SL is an opaque resident corporation subject to Impuesto sobre Sociedades (Ley 27/2014) at the standard 25% rate on worldwide income; no pass-through; territorial scope is worldwide for resident SLs (Territorial_Scope applies only to non-resident sellers). Tax_Exempt_Zone: not applicable, except for the optional Canary Islands ZEC special regime which is outside peninsular standard rules.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box; Spanish company-law characterisation is fixed. Available elections and regimes: (i) filing of Form 036/037 to exercise census and VAT-group elections (Régimen de Grupo de Entidades) where 50%+ control exists; (ii) election of the EU OSS/IOSS regimes for distance sales of goods; (iii) ETVE (holding company) election and 95% participation exemption for qualifying foreign shareholdings; (iv) simplified export customs procedures and authorised-economic-operator status; (v) reduced withholding via treaty relief certificates. Hybrid-mismatch rules (ATAD, Law 11/2021) and CFC rules are mandatory where triggered and cannot be opted out.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: IVA - Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido (Spanish Value Added Tax, Ley 37/1992 and Royal Decree 1624/1992, aligned with EU Directive 2006/112/EC).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No de-minimis turnover threshold: any established taxable person must register with AEAT (Form 036/037) before commencing the commercial activity and obtain a VAT-NIF. For non-established EU suppliers the intra-EU distance-sales threshold is EUR 10,000 per calendar year; at or above that figure registration in Spain or OSS election is mandatory. For purely domestic distance sales the threshold is EUR 35,000 (Art. 108 LIVA); cross-border B2B supplies have no threshold and require the buyer's Spanish VAT number.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No country-wide real-time stamping similar to Latin American clearance models. Mandatory SII (Suministro Inmediato de Información) applies to taxpayers with turnover above EUR 6,010,121.04, VAT groups and REDEME members: the issued and received invoice registers must be transmitted to AEAT through web services (API/XML in Facturae format) within 4 calendar days from issuance/booking (aggregate 8-day window), attracting fines for late or incorrect submission. Ley 18/2022 (Crea y Crece) and Royal Decree 1007/2023 will extend B2B electronic invoicing to all entrepreneurs/professionals (operative deadline pending) and require certified invoicing software ('Verifactu') with hash codes and AEAT-issued QR codes, effectively creating a digital audit/clearance integrity layer.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Export of goods (including organic dried goji berries and herbal botanicals) to third-country destinations qualifies as exempt with credit (0% VAT) under Art. 21 LIVA where: (i) the goods physically leave the EU customs territory within 90 days (3 months) from supply; (ii) the SL is the recorded exporter on the DUA and the customs office confirms exit; (iii) the commercial invoice, packing list and transport contract unambiguously identify the non-EU buyer and the consignment; (iv) export proceeds are received from that non-EU buyer in accordance with the foreign-exchange settlement rules; (v) the goods are not subject to deferred delivery or processing in the EU. Services directly linked to the export (freight, handling, insurance) are also zero-rated. Intra-EU B2B supplies under Art. 25 LIVA require the customer's valid EU VAT ID and removal documentation.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DUA / Single Administrative Document) validated by the Spanish customs office, including the movement reference number (MRN) and proof of physical exit from EU territory.
Bill of Lading (B/L) or Air Waybill (AWB) naming the SL as shipper and evidencing delivery to the third-country buyer at the destination port/airport.
Inward Remittance Certificate - SWIFT MT103 or Banco de España foreign-exchange settlement record demonstrating collection of the export price from the non-resident buyer.
Commercial invoice and packing list in the name of the SL, showing the HS classification for dried goji berries and herbal botanicals, consistent with the DUA data.
Supporting documents: certificate of origin, phytosanitary certificate for plant products, transport contract (CIF/CPT) and export insurance certificate.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: AEAT may scrutinise export zero-rating within the 4-year statute of limitations (10-year period for hidden transactions). Failure to substantiate the export leads to retroactive VAT assessment at 21% plus default interest (interés de demora), late-payment surcharges (5-20% graduated), and penalties under Arts. 191-198 LGT of 50% to 150% of the tax affected, aggravated to 100-150% for falsified customs transport documentation or unjustified refunds. Criminal liability under Art. 305 Criminal Code (Delito contra la Hacienda Pública) applies where the defrauded amount exceeds EUR 120,000, carrying imprisonment of 1-5 years, fines and loss of public benefits; directors are jointly and severally liable. The 180-day parameter follows the dossier template; note that Banco de España Circular 2/2017 sets a 115-day settlement benchmark for export collections, with declarations of 'exportaciones no cobradas' required after that date - although failure to collect within 115 days does not, per se, annul a VAT export exemption where shipment is proven, it increases audit scrutiny and may trigger a presumption that the sale was not a genuine export.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain operates a fully convertible Euro currency regime within the Eurozone. Capital account transactions are generally unrestricted for EU residents, with profit remittances subject only to standard corporate tax compliance and beneficial ownership declarations. Non-resident investors are subject to standard reporting obligations under Spanish foreign exchange and AML regulations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export proceeds must be repatriated to Spain within 30 days of collection. No mandatory surrender to the central bank or conversion ratios apply; however, all export transactions require prior statistical declaration via the SIEF (Integrated Foreign Trade System) administered by the Bank of Spain. Companies must retain documentary evidence of repatriation for audit and compliance verification.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasible for Spanish-licensed electronic money institutions under the Markets in Crypto-Assets (MiCA) framework, but cross-border digital EMIs face stringent licensing, capital, and operational requirements from the Bank of Spain; offshore EMIs are prohibited for Spanish corporate entities without local authorization.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence of directors is not mandatory for onboarding Spanish SL entities; remote KYC via video conferencing and digital signatures is permitted under Bank of Spain guidelines, provided all supporting documents are apostilled where required.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of funds originating from high-risk jurisdictions or inconsistent with declared business activity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed export contracts, phytosanitary certificates, commercial invoices, bank references, beneficial ownership certificates, and source-of-funds affidavits

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexplained large cash deposits or unusual transaction patterns
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Reconciliation statements, trade financing agreements, proof of legitimate business transactions, and matching documentation under UCP 600

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound capital injections routed via SWIFT MT103 wires denominated in EUR to the Spanish operational account. Purpose codes must specify 'Capital Contribution' or 'Share Capital Injection' accompanied by shareholder resolutions, incorporation documents, and tax identification numbers. All transactions undergo enhanced due diligence under Spanish AML/CFT regulations.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements processed through SWIFT MT103 for direct payments or Commercial Letters of Credit (LCs) under UCP 600. Clearing rails include correspondent banking networks with verification of documents such as invoices and packing lists. All settlements require document matching and compliance with anti-money laundering controls.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Forward FX contracts for EUR exposure management
Currency swaps for multi-currency trade settlements
Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) for hedging non-EUR export receivables

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: One month after approval by the Board of Directors
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines between 3,000 and 300,000 EUR; possible administrative dissolution

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 25 July following the end of the fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties of up to 20,000 EUR plus interest

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually or upon material changes in ownership

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit if the company exceeds two of the following: net turnover exceeding 2 million EUR, total assets exceeding 1 million EUR, or average number of employees exceeding 50
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish General Accounting Plan for non-qualifying entities; IFRS for public interest entities or larger companies

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annual confirmation and update of ultimate beneficial owner information in the beneficial ownership register

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 1,000 to 10,000 USD per year depending on audit complexity

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% general Corporate Income Tax (Impuesto sobre Sociedades, Le 27/2014, Art. 29.1); reduced 15% rate for newly created Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada in the first two tax periods with a positive taxable base (Art. 29.3 LIS).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 15% newly-established-entity rate; R&D and technological innovation tax credits (25% of qualifying R&D expenses; additional 17% for R&D staff increase; 8% innovation); participation exemption on qualifying dividends and capital gains (95% under Art. 21 LIS); international double taxation relief credits; minimum tax floor of 15% of the taxable base for entities with net turnover ≥ EUR 20 million (Art. 30bis LIS).
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Indefinite/unlimited carryforward for tax losses generated in tax periods commencing on or after 1 January 2015 (Art. 26.1 LIS); pre-2015 losses carryforward limited to 15 years. Annual offset is capped: 50% of taxable base for entities with net turnover ≥ EUR 20 million; 60% for net turnover between EUR 1 million and EUR 20 million; entities with turnover below EUR 1 million may offset in full, subject to a guaranteed minimum offset of EUR 1 million in the applicable bands.
